title: Denmark – Electrical installation work – El-installatørydelser til Aalborg Universitet
description: AAU ønsker med dette udbud at indgå en aftale med en primær og sekundær aktør. Den primære aktør anvendes i følgende situationer: A. Arbejdsopgaver inden for El-installationer, jf. aftalens pkt. 3.3. B. Arbejdsopgaver inden for brandtekniske installationer, jf. aftalens pkt. 3.3 (dog ikke f.s.v.a delaftale for København) C. Årligt eftersyn samt service og vedligehold på forskellige typer brandtekniske installationer, jf. aftalens pkt. 3.3 Den sekundære aktør anvendes i følgende situationer i henhold til aftalens: A. Arbejdsopgaver inden for El-installationer, jf. aftalens pkt. 3.3. B. Arbejdsopgaver inden for brandtekniske installationer, jf. aftalens pkt. 3.3 Ydelser i henhold til Aftalen udføres som udgangspunkt ved den primære leverandør, dog kan udførelse af ydelser ved den sekundære leverandør blive relevant i følgende situationer: • Hvis den primære leverandør ikke kan udføre en ydelse som følge af forbigående forhindringer, såsom mandskabsmangel eller andet, kan bestillingen i stedet gå til den sekundære leverandør. • Hvis AAU har fastsat en tidsfrist for færdiggørelse af en konkret opgave, og den primære leverandør ikke kan tilbyde at udføre ydelsen inden den af AAU fastsatte tidsfrist, kan ydelsen i stedet udføres af den sekundære leverandør. • Hvis den primære leverandør væsentligt misligholder Aftalen, kan AAU ophæve Aftalen med denne leverandør, hvorefter den sekundære leverandør bliver den primære leverandør af alle ydelser i henhold til aftalen. De beskrevne situationer dækker over, at AAU ønsker en fast samarbejdspartner i form af en primær leverandør, som ikke blot kan udføre service og vedligehold af el- og brandinstallationer, men også kan anvendes til større opgaver inden for disse arbejder. AAU ønsker i tillæg til dette at have en fast samarbejdspartner i form af en sekundær leverandør, som kan sikre driften i tilfælde af, at den primære leverandør ikke kan dette – nærmere bestemt i de tilfælde, der er oplistet i aftalens pkt. 3.2. Aftalerne træder i kraft den 1. december 2026 og udløber uden varsel den 30. november 2031. Der kan ske forlængelse i op til 2 år. Kontraktstart den 1. december 2026 forudsætter, at der ikke opstår forsinkelser. Det kan derfor ikke udelukkes, at kontraktstart vil blive udskudt, hvis der opstår forsinkelser i relation til gennemførelse af udbuddet. I givet fald vil udløbsdatoen blive fremrykket tilsvarende.

description: SUBJECT: AOI 3 Space Intelligence � Third Call for Submissions Under the Notice ID FA8806-26-S-0001 (01 July 2026) Kronos Family of Systems (FoS) Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) 1. Purpose: This document constitutes the Third Call under the Kronos FoS CSO. Refer to the Kronos FoS CSO 2.0 for all administrative, legal, and overarching procedures. 2. This Call specifically requests Phase 1A (Quad Chart and White Paper) submissions to address Area of Interest (AOI) 3, and its Focus Area Statements (FAS) detailed below. 3. FAS #1 (AOI 03-FAS01): The SSC SYD 85 Kronos Program seeks an enterprise collection management orchestration capability to coherently link existing sensor optimization and scheduling capabilities for sensing of the space domain. The capability focuses on the optimal use of finite sensors to meet collection requirements that fulfill positional tracking, operational intelligence, and foundational intelligence needs. This effort will focus not only on USSF sensors but also establish interfaces with other DoW, Intelligence Community (IC), allied, and commercial assets. A successful orchestration �brain� must demonstrate the ability to integrate multiple orchestration engines utilizing distinct scheduling paradigms (e.g., pre-planned, dynamic tip-and-cue event response, automated metric optimization), rapidly adjudicate scheduling conflicts when dynamic tasks out-prioritize deliberate needs, and disseminate commander decisions to sensors, sensor brokers, and external orchestration platforms. The capability shall consider weather, planned and unplanned outages, multiple sensor phenomenologies, tasking acknowledgment response times, PED and correlation timelines, competing prioritization schemes, and the ability to monitor execution during dynamic events. Furthermore, the proposed solution must deliver intuitive user feedback regarding collection requirement satisfaction (with full traceability), candidate rescheduling options for human review, human-in-the-loop intervention, and transparent performance metrics. A successful solution shall provide a rapid path for a prototype to host on Secret and Top Secret domains to interface with existing tasking engines and sensors. 4. FAS #2 (AOI 03-FAS02): The SSC SYD 85 Kronos Program seeks innovative commercial solutions and products addressing the ability to ingest and analyze radar and sensor data for characterization of on-orbit assets. Capability should allow support analysis of radar cross sections, object discrimination and velocity and maneuver determination. 5. FAS #3 (AOI 03-FAS03): The SSC SYD 85 Kronos Program seeks innovative commercial solutions and products addressing novel or innovative ways to ingest and analyze commercial RF data and distribution of data to operations centers to support object maneuver detection, status assessments, and object identification efforts. 6. FAS #4 (AOI 03-FAS04): The SSC SYD 85 Kronos Program seeks innovative commercial solutions and products addressing deployment of capabilities to the tactical edge, using novel or innovative methodologies to transport data back to operations centers. Solutions should demonstrate the ability to operate through disconnected connectivity and demonstrate re-sync of data once re-connected. 7. FAS #5 (AOI 3-FAS05): The SSC SYD 85 Kronos Program and its stakeholders seek innovative commercial solutions and products which enable immediate reporting of space events to the U.S. Space Command Joint Operations Center. This capability will collate all event knowledge as it�s occurring to provide Combatant Commanders, Joint Staff, and National Leadership situational awareness, real-time updates, and response options for approval. The system must be able to support both coalition space event conferences and U.S. -only space event conferences. 8. Offerors may submit more than one white paper and quad chart for this call and any future call. The white paper and quad chart proposed prototype solution may address one or more focus areas; but it must be clear in the proposed solution how the proposed prototype addresses the AOI and which focus areas. 9. Submission Timeline: Questions regarding this Call shall be submitted no later than 1200 Pacific Time on 09 September 2026. Phase 1A submissions (Quad Chart and White Paper) shall be received no later than 1700 Pacific Time on 25 September 2026. 10. Additional Information: All submission instructions, eligibility requirements, evaluation procedures, and applicable terms and conditions are contained within the Kronos FoS CSO. Offerors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov (http://sam.gov) for amendments, answers to questions, and any updates associated with this Call.

description: SUBJECT: AOI 3 Space Intelligence � Third Call for Submissions Under the Notice ID FA8806-26-S-0001 (01 July 2026) Kronos Family of Systems (FoS) Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) 1. Purpose: This document constitutes the Third Call under the Kronos FoS CSO. Refer to the Kronos FoS CSO 2.0 for all administrative, legal, and overarching procedures. 2. This Call specifically requests Phase 1A (Quad Chart and White Paper) submissions to address Area of Interest (AOI) 3, and its Focus Area Statements (FAS) detailed below. 3. FAS #1 (AOI 03-FAS01): The SSC SYD 85 Kronos Program seeks an enterprise collection management orchestration capability to coherently link existing sensor optimization and scheduling capabilities for sensing of the space domain. The capability focuses on the optimal use of finite sensors to meet collection requirements that fulfill positional tracking, operational intelligence, and foundational intelligence needs. This effort will focus not only on USSF sensors but also establish interfaces with other DoW, Intelligence Community (IC), allied, and commercial assets. A successful orchestration �brain� must demonstrate the ability to integrate multiple orchestration engines utilizing distinct scheduling paradigms (e.g., pre-planned, dynamic tip-and-cue event response, automated metric optimization), rapidly adjudicate scheduling conflicts when dynamic tasks out-prioritize deliberate needs, and disseminate commander decisions to sensors, sensor brokers, and external orchestration platforms. The capability shall consider weather, planned and unplanned outages, multiple sensor phenomenologies, tasking acknowledgment response times, PED and correlation timelines, competing prioritization schemes, and the ability to monitor execution during dynamic events. Furthermore, the proposed solution must deliver intuitive user feedback regarding collection requirement satisfaction (with full traceability), candidate rescheduling options for human review, human-in-the-loop intervention, and transparent performance metrics. A successful solution shall provide a rapid path for a prototype to host on Secret and Top Secret domains to interface with existing tasking engines and sensors. 4. FAS #2 (AOI 03-FAS02): The SSC SYD 85 Kronos Program seeks innovative commercial solutions and products addressing the ability to ingest and analyze radar and sensor data for characterization of on-orbit assets. Capability should allow support analysis of radar cross sections, object discrimination and velocity and maneuver determination. 5. FAS #3 (AOI 03-FAS03): The SSC SYD 85 Kronos Program seeks innovative commercial solutions and products addressing novel or innovative ways to ingest and analyze commercial RF data and distribution of data to operations centers to support object maneuver detection, status assessments, and object identification efforts. 6. FAS #4 (AOI 03-FAS04): The SSC SYD 85 Kronos Program seeks innovative commercial solutions and products addressing deployment of capabilities to the tactical edge, using novel or innovative methodologies to transport data back to operations centers. Solutions should demonstrate the ability to operate through disconnected connectivity and demonstrate re-sync of data once re-connected. 7. FAS #5 (AOI 3-FAS05): The SSC SYD 85 Kronos Program and its stakeholders seek innovative commercial solutions and products which enable immediate reporting of space events to the U.S. Space Command Joint Operations Center. This capability will collate all event knowledge as it�s occurring to provide Combatant Commanders, Joint Staff, and National Leadership situational awareness, real-time updates, and response options for approval. The system must be able to support both coalition space event conferences and U.S. -only space event conferences. 8. Offerors may submit more than one white paper and quad chart for this call and any future call. The white paper and quad chart proposed prototype solution may address one or more focus areas; but it must be clear in the proposed solution how the proposed prototype addresses the AOI and which focus areas. 9. Submission Timeline: Questions regarding this Call shall be submitted no later than 1200 Pacific Time on 09 September 2026. Phase 1A submissions (Quad Chart and White Paper) shall be received no later than 1700 Pacific Time on 25 September 2026. 10. title: PEO-FW Group 2 Air-Launched Effects (A2E) Assessment Event (AE)
description: PEO-FW Group 2 Air-Launched Effects (A2E) Assessment Event (AE) Submit NLT 25 September 2026 11:59 PM ET U.S. Citizens Only Purpose SOFWERX, in collaboration with the USSOCOM Program Executive Office Fixed Wing (PEO-FW), will host an Assessment Event (AE) to identify potential vendors to integrate existing compatible small, unmanned air system (sUAS) platforms into a Karman Systima Common Launch Tube (CLT). This event aims to accelerate capability insertion for platform systems to be quickly integrated into the CLT system for the purpose of launching Group 2 sUAS. Background/Synopsis The Adaptive Airborne Enterprise (A2E) is an interoperable system of systems designed to enable robust ISR capabilities through expendable, autonomous sUAS platforms, resilient data paths, and a common control architecture. FANTOM Core-enabled sUAS platforms are typically launched using the Karman Systima CLT system. Objective The objective of this assessment event is to gather information on the integration capabilities of TRL 5+ sUAS into the Karman Systima CLT for Air-Launched Effects (ALE). Specifically, the Government seeks to identify airframes capable of rapid integration into the Karman Systima Space & Defense CLT to support Find, Fix, Track, Target (F2T2) and Electronic Warfare (EW) missions under the Air Force Special Operations Command (AFSOC) A2E program. Why You Should Participate USSOCOM seeks to enter into non-FAR or FAR-based agreements with Industry, Academic, and National Lab partners whose solutions are favorably evaluated by PEO-FW Subject Matter Experts (SMEs). As such, the follow-on Assessment Event (AE) is considered competitive, and solutions will be evaluated independently of one another primarily for technical merit. This serves dually as notification of the intent to research the feasibility of an agreement under 10 U.S. Code, Section 4022 and/or Section 4022(f), and as notice of pre-solicitation activities IAW FAR 5.204. Event Timeline Phase 1 - 25 August 2026 to 25 September 2026 Submissions to the Assessment Event (AE) Open: Interested respondents who could potentially provide solutions that meet the needs of USSOCOM are encouraged to submit their capability for USSOCOM review. To submit your technology for potential Phase 3 attendance, please review the assessment criteria and follow the submission instructions at the bottom of this webpage. Phase 1a - 02 September 2026 Q&A Telecon: Interested offerors may participate in a virtual Q&A session to better understand the PM's specific technology objectives. The telecon will take place on 02 September from 1:00�2:00 PM ET. RSVP at the bottom of this webpage. Phase 2 - 28 September 2026 to 09 October 2026 Downselect: USSOCOM will downselect those respondents/submissions they feel have the highest potential to satisfy their technology needs. Favorably evaluated submissions will receive an invitation to attend the AE on/around 12 October. Phase 3 - 27 October 2026 Assessment Event (AE): During the AE, selected participants will be allotted a one-on-one session with the USSOCOM evaluation panel to pitch, demonstrate, and/or discuss their solutions. The forum will include a Q&A portion and discussions may continue outside of the event. Solution brief presentation guidelines will be outlined in the event invitation and solutions will be assessed according to the criteria in the link provided below. If the USSOCOM evaluation panel favorably evaluates a solution brief, negotiations for Phase 4 may immediately begin. This event will be held virtually via Microsoft Teams. Phase 4 - Path Forward: Successfully negotiated awards may fall under any combination of these categories: Business to business research and development agreement as a sub-award through the SOFWERX Partnership Intermediary Agreement (PIA) (15 U.S. Code Section 3715) OTA for research or prototype projects (10 U.S. Code Sections 4021, 4022) An award under 10 U. The Government may make this follow-on production award based upon successful prototype criteria, which will be determined for each prototype project. description: 1. INTRODUCTION & PURPOSE This Special Notice is issued solely for market research, information, and planning purposes�it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or Invitation for Bid (IFB). There is no commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation, make awards, or pay for any costs incurred by respondents in preparing responses to this notice. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Europe District (NAU) querying the commercial marketplace to gauge industry capabilities, technical maturity, commercial availability, and execution strategies regarding Industrialized Construction (IC) and alternative construction methodologies. The objective of this market survey is to obtain strategic industry feedback to operationalize recent Department of the Army policy directives aimed at accelerating infrastructure delivery, reducing initial capital costs, and increasing real property portfolio flexibility. 2. BACKGROUND & STRATEGIC INTENT In accordance with the Department of the Army Memorandum (Facility Construction Policy Implementing Installation Resilience through Industrialized Construction (IC) Methodologies), the Army is transforming how it plans, designs, and constructs facility assets. Traditional design-bid-build processes and on-site construction methods are too slow and costly to keep pace with modem operational requirements. The intent is to accelerate the delivery of critical infrastructure, reduce initial capital costs, and increase the flexibility of the Army's real property portfolio to meet rapidly evolving warfighter requirements. Historically, Army facilities have been engineered for 50-year lifespans, often becoming functionally obsolete before structurally deficient. Moving forward, facilities will be designed to optimize an approximately 25-year lifespan. This provides strategic agility to align with supported platforms and enables rapid recapitalization by allowing structures to be repurposed or relocated as missions change. As a result, the Army seeks to transition to modern Industrialized Construction methodologies targeting: 50% faster delivery timeline compared to traditional construction. 30% reduction in initial capital costs. Optimization for an approximate 25-year facility lifespan (moving away from traditional 50-year engineering baselines) to enable strategic agility, rapid recapitalization, repurposing, or relocation as operational missions evolve. 3. TOPICS OF INTEREST: IC METHODOLOGIES & FACILITY APPLICATIONS NAU is specifically seeking industry capabilities and technical feedback regarding five (5) primary alternative construction methodologies (Ref: ASA IE&E Memo, Para 3.a�e) as applied to three (3) key facility categories (Ref: ASA IE&E Memo, Para 5.a�c), though application to other repeatable facility types is also welcomed. A. Directed Alternative Construction Methodologies (Memo Para 3.a�e) Volumetric Modular Construction: Off-site manufactured three-dimensional volumetric units transported and assembled on-site. Kit of Parts (Panelized) / Pre-Cast Systems: Prefabricated components, wall panels, and structural assemblies designed for specific building configurations. Pre-Engineered Metal Buildings (PEMB): Standardized, scalable steel structural systems. Tension Fabric Structures (TFS): Rapidly deployable aluminum or steel-framed engineered fabric structures. Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing): Automated, on-site or near-site concrete/composite 3D printing systems. B. Primary Target Facility Applications (Memo Para 5.a�c) Category 1: Aircraft Hangars (Para 5.a) Primary Focus: Application of Tension Fabric Structures (TFS) providing clear-span workspaces and environmental protection, erected in a fraction of traditional construction timelines. Category 2: Maintenance Facilities (Para 5.b) Primary Focus: Application of Pre-Engineered Metal Buildings (PEMB) or Panelized Steel Structures capable of supporting heavy-duty overhead cranes while standardizing procurement and accelerating erection. Category 3: Barracks, Child Development Centers (CDCs), Kennels, & Repeatable Buildings (Para 5.c) Primary Focus: Application of Volumetric Modular Construction, Kit of Parts, or Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing) offering high off-site quality control, enhanced thermal performance, and rapid occupancy turnaround. 4. CORE CAPABILITY & EXPERIENCE INQUIRIES ("THE PULSE") Interested sources are requested to provide clear, concise responses to the following core inquiries: Section A: Firm Overview & Strategic Alignment General Capability: Briefly describe your firm�s primary business model, technical focus, manufacturing capacity (if applicable), and experience operating as a prime contractor or key technology partner in Industrialized Construction. Target Scope & Capacity: What is your firm�s ideal project scale (e.g., square footage, dollar value, or unit volume per year) for delivering IC solutions? Section B: Technical Evaluation of Methodologies (Memo 3.a�e vs 5.a�c) Methodology Alignment: Detail your firm�s specific capabilities and execution track record in one or more of the following: -Volumetric Modular -Kit of Parts / Panelized Pre-Cast -Pre-Engineered Metal Buildings (PEMB) -Tension Fabric Structures (TFS) -Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing) Facility Application & Suitability: How well do your IC methodologies integrate with the designated facility types (Hangars, Maintenance Shops, Barracks/CDCs/Repeatable Structures)? What technical modifications or building code considerations are critical for DoD adoption? Are there other facility types that are not included in this announcement that your firm believes would be good candidates for IC methodologies? 25-Year Lifespan & Flexibility Optimization: With the Department of War�s stated objective of reducing the expected lifespan of these facilities to be constructed from 50 years to 25 years in order to achieve lower investment and maintenance costs, do you believe that the IC construction methodologies contemplated by this memorandum are viable delivery methods to meet the 25 year life span expectation? How do the IC methodology capabilities that your company possesses a 25-year optimized lifecycle? Discuss disassembly, relocation, structural repurposing, and recapitalization advantages of your system compared to traditional 50-year brick-and-mortar builds. Section C: Cost, Schedule, & Delivery Optimization Speed & Cost Metrics: How can your firm achieve or approach the Army's benchmark goals of 50% faster delivery and a 30% cost reduction? Supply Chain & Logistics: What are the key supply chain, manufacturing lead time, or transportation constraints associated with scaling your IC methodology across domestic (CONUS) and/or overseas (OCONUS) military installations? Contracting & Delivery Models: What project delivery models best support your manufacturing and installation workflows? Section D: Sourced Experience & Project History Provide up to three (3) representative project examples completed within the past five (5) years demonstrating successful implementation of IC methodologies. For each project, specify: Facility type and delivery methodology utilized (from Para 3.a�e). Timeline comparison (design/fabrication/erection time vs traditional estimated baseline). Cost performance and life-cycle/re-use features. Key lessons learned and recommendations for Government adoption. 5. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Firms possessing the capability, experience, and interest in supporting the Army's Industrialized Construction policy are invited to submit their responses in accordance with the following parameters: Response Parameters: Page Limit: Not to exceed ten (10) pages total (including cover page and attachments). Format: Microsoft Word (.docx) or Adobe PDF (.pdf) format, standard 12-pt font. description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a solicitation for bids, proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of all qualified sources to perform a potential requirement. The responses received from interested contractors will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 20, is conducting market research to identify potential sources which can provide the following services: Title: Panic and Intrusion Alarm Replacement and Monitoring NAICS Code: 561621, Security Systems Services (except Locksmiths) Locations: Fairview VA Clinic, 1800 NE Market Drive, Fairview, OR 97024 Hillsboro VA Clinic,1925 NE Stucki Ave, 3rd and 4th Floor, Hillsboro, OR, 97006 West Linn VA Clinic, 1750 SW Blankenship Road, Suite 300, West Linn, OR 97068 The Dalles CBOC, 704 Veterans Drive, The Dalles, OR 97058 Bend CBOC, 2650 NE Courtney Drive, Bend, OR, 97701 Salem CBOC, 1750 McGilchrist Street SE, Salem, OR 97302 Tasks: Within 30 days, upon award of the contract, the contractor shall remove, install, and test all new components at each location. This should include, keypads, panels, motion sensors, and wireless panic alarms, to the quantity provided at each location. Motion sensors must be based off of PIR and/or Microwave Technology. Sensors should range in detection distance of 40 to 200 feet depending on the area being covered. Some areas will require 360-degree sensors due to cross areas. Sensors should comprise of anti-masking technology where available. Once installed, Contractor shall provide alarm monitoring 24/7. All Security Systems and components must have the ability to be live tested with the monitoring station every month. This will include individual panic alarms, motion sensors, door contacts, and any other form of input. All systems must have the ability to accept multiple access codes with only one master code. The system should have the ability to track which codes were used to arm and disarm the system. The system should have the capability to be armed and disarmed with the use of a proximity card or key fob. With the possible potential to use HSPD-12 compliant ID cards, commonly known as VA PIV Badges or CAC Cards. The government should have the ability to log into the systems remotely to arm, disarm, and view activity history remotely. Contractor shall reply to repair requests within 4 hours of call. All repairs must be completed within 5 days. If not the contractor needs to supply a detailed action plan and any mitigations Period of Performance: Estimate 12/1/2025-11/30/2026 plus Option Years 1-4. Potential candidates having the capabilities necessary to provide the above stated services are invited to respond to this Sources Sought Notice via e-mail to Danielle Carrico at Danielle.Carrico@va.gov no later than 9/26/2025 at 5PM PT. The Government will treat any information received as proprietary and will not share such information with other companies. Any organization responding to this Sources Sought Notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization's qualifications to perform the work. The United States Department Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Research Service (ARS), supported by the R8 Procurement and Property Support Services Division, Region 8 US Forest Service, CSA 11, intends to award on a single source basis. Purchase order type will be a Firm Fixed Price awarded to Alleghany Farm Services. This requirement is for the purchase of professional agricultural drainage construction services to install, repair, and improve subsurface drainage tile systems at the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Research Service (ARS), Plant Genetic Resources Unit located at 2862 County Road 6, Geneva, New York 14456. The work includes field surveying, installation of new drainage tile, connection to existing drainage infrastructure, installation of drainage outlets and rodent guards, and use of specialized equipment to install drainage tile within vineyard and specialty crop research fields. These improvements are needed to reduce waterlogged conditions, improve soil drainage and field access, increase the amount of usable agricultural land, and support plant genetic resource conservation, regeneration, and agricultural research activities conducted at the facility. This project is essential to support the mission of the United States Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research Service, Plant Genetic Resources Unit by ensuring that agricultural research and germplasm regeneration fields remain accessible, productive, and suitable for crop production. The installation and improvement of subsurface drainage systems will reduce standing water and waterlogged soil conditions that currently limit planting, cultivation, maintenance, and harvesting operations. If this project is completed, poorly drained areas will continue to experience excessive soil moisture, resulting in reduced field accessibility, delayed planting and harvest operations, increased soil compaction, and degraded growing conditions. These conditions will negatively impact germplasm regeneration activities, research trials, and field-based plant breeding programs by reducing crop establishment, increasing the risk of crop loss, and compromising the quality and reliability of research data. Failure to complete the drainage improvements will also reduce the amount of usable agricultural land available for research and regeneration activities, limiting the Plant Genetic Resources Unit's capacity to maintain, regenerate, and distribute plant genetic resources. Continued deterioration of drainage conditions may result in increased maintenance costs, additional crop losses, and long-term reductions in operational efficiency. The project is therefore mission essential to maintaining critical agricultural research infrastructure and supporting the conservation and utilization of plant genetic resources entrusted to the Agricultural Research Service.

description: Advance Procurement Notice Construction of Temporary Modular Workspaces Kingston, ON (with Security Requirements) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Approximately 23,000 sq ft over 5 buildings. This work includes, but is not limited to: Prefabrication of building modules off site; Completion of civil works, site servicing and wood crib foundations to prepare the site for assembly and construction of modular office buildings; Delivery to site and assembly of prefabricated modules into temporary modular buildings; Tie-ins to existing utilities and the construction of a new access road on the site; and  Finish construction and outfitting of the modular office buildings on site. The solicitation process will start with a Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) as the first step of a two-step process, the second step being the Tender Phase.  Only the general contractors who will have responded to this RFEOI will be invited to submit a bid during the Tender Phase. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or bidder regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent or bidder will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. The chase crew is responsible for uninterrupted visual scanning, collision avoidance, maintaining communication with both the RPA and Air Traffic Control (ATC), Contractor-Furnished Aircraft & Equipment Requirements Performance: Capable of a sustained speed of 150 knots true airspeed at an altitude of 12,000 feet and below. Onboard Equipment: Chase and RPA will operate beacons and strobe lights during both day and night operations. General Flight Operations Takeoff & Transit: The chase aircraft shall be overhead March ARB (KRIV) at the scheduled RPA takeoff time. The chase will accompany the RPA during pattern operations and transit to restricted airspace (R-2515 or R-2503) per the current COA and LOA. After drop-off, the chase will return to base and remain on standby. Recovery: The chase aircraft will report to the designated pick-up point (R-2515 or R-2503) 10 minutes prior to the scheduled handover time and orbit. Upon clearance, the chase will rejoin the RPA and escort it back to KRIV, remaining in formation until the RPA completes a full-stop landing. Transfer of Control: The chase will maintain visual responsibility until the RPA enters the KRIV traffic pattern and a ground observer officially takes over visual responsibilities. Chase Observer: Responsible for clearing for traffic and advising the RPA of potential conflicts or deteriorating weather. Possess a current airman medical certificate (FAA Class 2 or military equivalent) per 14 CFR 67. Must be current per 14 CFR 61.56 (Flight Review) and 61.57 (Recent Flight Experience). Shall comply with 14 CFR 91.17 regarding alcohol and drug use. Observer Qualifications: Must have a comprehensive understanding of federal aviation regulations for the operational airspace.
